signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5968 trades with significant momentum, outperforming as the clear G10 leader with a 1W average of +1.079% across its peer group. The spread between NZD and the laggard USD has widened to 2.353%, marking a strong bilateral theme as US yields pull back and Fed hike bets recede. This move is fundamentally anchored by the RBNZ's hiking stance and a deeply accommodative real rate of -1.56% (2.5% policy vs 4.06% inflation expectations), while the USD ESI of -15.1 confirms persistent data misses. Technically, the pair is holding firmly above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5869/0.5797/0.5840), confirming a structural bullish breakout. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD; G10 divergence and technical breakout support trend extension. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — 2.5% rate and hike bias in focus. Risk: Sharp reversal in US yields challenges the 'Bessent put' and compresses the G10 spread.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Positioning + Vol + Retail Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3646, positioned well above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3468/1.3391/1.3424). Leveraged funds are net long +42,722 (90th percentile), indicating a crowded institutional long position that aligns with a 1M 4W WoW delta of +3,683. However, the options market is pricing in significant caution with a +5.0% Vol Risk Premium (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.0%), suggesting heavy demand for protection against a move away from current levels. Retail sentiment has reached an 85% short extreme, providing a contrarian signal that institutional longs may still have room to squeeze retail before the trend exhausts. While the BoE and Fed are both on hold at 3.75%, the UK 10Y yield of 5.06% maintains a +36bp spread over the US 10Y, providing underlying support. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD; retail short-squeeze potential offsets crowded institutional positioning. Catalyst: Flash PMIs today. Risk: UK retail sales miss (-0.5%) triggers a broader fundamental repricing that forces an institutional long unwind.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + Correlation Break
signals.text: USD/JPY is testing 158.91, holding just above the SMA200 at 158.30 while remaining below shorter-term averages. Despite a significant 275bp carry advantage for the USD based on Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% rates, the options market is aggressively hedging for downside with a strong -2.02 Risk Reversal skew. This bearish options bias is compounded by a correlation break between USD/JPY and the VIX (z=+1.85σ), signaling that the pair is no longer reacting to volatility in its traditional safe-haven capacity. The JPY ESI at +22.3 vs USD at -15.1 suggests a macro-data tailwind for the Yen even as specs remain net short -59,526. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options market hedging downside despite the carry advantage. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias 1.0% policy. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 re-engages carry demand and triggers BoJ intervention warnings.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Extreme + Commodity Bid
signals.text: AUD/USD at 0.7147 maintains a bullish posture above all major SMAs, supported by a 60bp carry advantage for AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%). Retail sentiment is at an 87% short extreme, diverging from the institutional trend and suggesting a high probability of further upside as retail shorts are forced to cover. Gold's rally to fresh highs above $4,550 provides a positive commodity-linked backdrop for the AUD, while the COT 52w percentile of 75 suggests positioning is not yet at an exhaustive extreme. The pair's 1W performance of +1.19% reflects this broad-based support. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; commodity strength and retail extreme support higher levels. Catalyst: US long-term yield moves and Jackson Hole sentiment. Risk: Sharp drop in gold prices or a hawk-tilt at the Fed reduces the carry-commodity appeal.
